article.title: Housewarming Drinks Gifts That Beat Flowers
article.body:
Housewarming Drinks Gifts That Beat Flowers

The best housewarming drinks gift pairs something to open on the first night, such as a bottle of champagne, with something that lasts, like glassware or a spirit for the new home bar. Drinks House 247 delivers gifts to new addresses across London, usually within 30 to 45 minutes, with a written gift note.

Flowers are a lovely gesture, but they arrive when the new owners are surrounded by boxes, have no idea which one holds the vase, and will be throwing them away in a week. A well-chosen bottle is more useful, lasts longer and marks the occasion properly.

What makes a good housewarming drinks gift?

The best ones do one of two jobs, and ideally both.

  • Something to open now. Moving day is exhausting. A chilled bottle to toast the first evening in the new place is the gift people remember.
  • Something to keep. A new home is a fresh start for the drinks cupboard. A good spirit, a set of proper glasses or a bottle worth saving for a first dinner party all stay with the household long after moving day.

Pairing the two, say a bottle of champagne with a pair of flutes, covers both jobs and looks generous without being excessive.

Ideas by type of household

The household Open now Keep for later
First-time buyers A non-vintage champagne or English sparkling wine Two champagne flutes or a pair of good tumblers
A couple who entertain A crowd-pleasing red and white for the first dinner A magnum to open at the housewarming party
Cocktail lovers A quality gin with its matching tonic A bottle to start the home bar: a good bourbon, vermouth or aged rum
Whisky drinkers A single malt they have not tried A whisky and glass gift set
A family with young children A bottle for the adults once the children are in bed A rosé or sparkling for the first summer in the garden
Someone who has everything A prestige or vintage champagne A gift hamper with chocolates or caviar

Should you choose champagne?

It is the traditional choice for a reason: the moment of opening a bottle in a new home is a small ceremony in itself. You do not need a prestige cuvée. A well-made non-vintage brut from a good house, served cold, does the job perfectly. If you want to spend more, a vintage champagne is a better housewarming gift than a pricier non-vintage, because it can be saved for a first anniversary in the home.

If the recipients do not drink much champagne, a good English sparkling wine or a bottle of a still wine they love is every bit as thoughtful.

Is glassware a good idea?

Often it is the most useful part of the gift. Glasses are among the first things to break in a move and the last things anyone thinks to replace. A pair of champagne flutes, whisky tumblers or large wine glasses is used for years. Gift sets that combine a bottle with matching glasses are the simplest way to do this well.

What to avoid

  • Anything too personal to your own taste. An intensely peated Islay whisky is a brilliant gift for someone who loves smoke and a baffling one for someone who does not.
  • Expecting it to be opened while you are there. A housewarming gift belongs to the hosts. Let them decide when to open it.
  • Very large formats for a small flat. A jeroboam is a showpiece, but in a one-bedroom flat with a small fridge it can be more burden than treat.

Why the gift note matters

A new home generates a stream of deliveries, and an unlabelled bottle can easily be mistaken for something the owners ordered themselves. A short written note, even two lines, makes sure the gift is credited to you and turns a bottle into a message. Mention the occasion, and if the bottle is for keeping, say so: "Save this for your first dinner party."

Sending it to the new address

You do not need to carry a bottle across London on moving day. You can send a gift straight to the new address:

  1. Use the full new address, including flat number and postcode. New-build developments and conversions often have confusing entrances, so add any access notes.
  2. Include the recipient's mobile number so the driver can reach them.
  3. Choose a time when someone is home. The day after the move is often better than the day itself.
  4. Remember that the person receiving it must be 18 or over and may be asked for ID under our Challenge 21 policy.

Frequently asked questions

What is a good housewarming gift instead of flowers?

A bottle of champagne or a good spirit, ideally paired with glassware. It gives the new owners something to open on the first night and something useful to keep.

Is champagne a good housewarming gift?

Yes. A well-made non-vintage brut is ideal for toasting the first evening, and a vintage champagne can be saved for a later occasion in the new home.

Can I send a housewarming gift to someone's new address?

Yes. Give the full new address with flat number, postcode and any access notes, plus a mobile number. The recipient must be 18 or over and may be asked for ID.

Should I write a note with a housewarming gift?

Yes. New homes receive many deliveries, and a short written note makes sure the gift is credited to you and explains whether it is for now or for keeping.

Choosing a gift

See our housewarming gift guide, or browse champagne gifts, champagne and flute sets and alcohol gift sets and hampers. For sending anywhere in the country, see how to send a gift across the UK.

Deliveries are to over-18s only under our Challenge 21 policy. Please drink responsibly.
article.summary: The best housewarming drinks gifts give something to open tonight and something to keep. Ideas by type of household, and how to send a gift to a new address.
